title: webhooks/mpesa: implement full M-Pesa STK Push callback parser
body:
## Summary
The `parseMpesaPayload` function in `src/webhooks/mpesa.ts` is a stub. It needs to handle the full M-Pesa STK Push callback schema, including nested `Body.stkCallback` fields.

## M-Pesa Callback Schema
```json
{
  "Body": {
    "stkCallback": {
      "MerchantRequestID": "...",
      "CheckoutRequestID": "...",
      "ResultCode": 0,
      "ResultDesc": "The service request is processed successfully.",
      "CallbackMetadata": {
        "Item": [
          { "Name": "Amount", "Value": 1 },
          { "Name": "MpesaReceiptNumber", "Value": "NLJ7RT61SV" },
          { "Name": "PhoneNumber", "Value": 254708374149 }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Implementation Steps
1. Update `parseMpesaPayload` to navigate `Body.stkCallback`.
2. Extract `Amount`, `MpesaReceiptNumber`, and `PhoneNumber` from `CallbackMetadata.Item`.
3. Map `ResultCode !== 0` to a failed/ignored state (return `null` or throw).
4. Export a `MpesaCallbackBody` TypeScript interface in `src/types/index.ts`.
5. Update the unit test in `tests/webhooks.test.ts` with the real schema.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Parser handles the full nested schema.
- [ ] `ResultCode !== 0` payloads are rejected with a descriptive error.
- [ ] TypeScript interface exported and used.
- [ ] Unit tests pass with `npm test`.
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes with no warnings.

title: webhooks/mtn: implement MTN MoMo payment notification parser
body:
## Summary
The `parseMtnPayload` stub in `src/webhooks/mtn.ts` does not handle the real MTN MoMo Collections API callback schema.

## MTN MoMo Callback Schema
```json
{
  "financialTransactionId": "363440463",
  "externalId": "947354",
  "amount": "100",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "payer": { "partyIdType": "MSISDN", "partyId": "46733123454" },
  "payerMessage": "Pay for product",
  "payeeNote": "Note",
  "status": "SUCCESSFUL"
}
```

## Implementation Steps
1. Update `parseMtnPayload` to map `financialTransactionId`, `payer.partyId`, and `status`.
2. Reject payloads where `status !== "SUCCESSFUL"`.
3. Export a `MtnCallbackBody` TypeScript interface.
4. Add a corresponding Airtel Money parser update in `src/webhooks/airtel.ts` for the `transaction.status` field.
5. Write unit tests for both success and failure status codes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both MTN and Airtel parsers handle their real schemas.
- [ ] Non-successful statuses are rejected.
- [ ] Interfaces exported and used throughout.
- [ ] Tests cover success and failure paths.

title: relayer: wire webhook handlers to the Stellar settlement relay
body:
## Summary
The webhook handlers in `src/webhooks/*.ts` currently return a stub JSON response. They need to call `relayToStellar` from `src/relayer/index.ts` and return the settlement result.

## Implementation Steps
1. In each handler (`mpesaWebhookHandler`, `mtnWebhookHandler`, `airtelWebhookHandler`):
   a. Parse the payload.
   b. Call `await relayToStellar(payload)`.
   c. If `result.success`, respond `202 Accepted` with `{ txHash }`.
   d. If `!result.success`, respond `500` with `{ error }`.
2. Make handlers `async`.
3. Add a global Express error handler in `src/app.ts` to catch unhandled promise rejections.
4. Write an integration test using `supertest` that mocks `relayToStellar` and asserts the correct HTTP response codes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three handlers call `relayToStellar` and return the correct HTTP status.
- [ ] Error path returns `500` with a JSON error body.
- [ ] Integration tests pass.
- [ ] No unhandled promise rejections.

title: middleware: implement per-provider HMAC signature verification
body:
## Summary
The `verifySignature` middleware in `src/middleware/verifySignature.ts` exists but is not wired to any route. Each provider uses a different header and hashing scheme.

## Provider Signature Schemes
| Provider | Header | Algorithm |
|---|---|---|
| M-Pesa | No standard header — use IP allowlist or shared secret in query param | HMAC-SHA256 |
| MTN MoMo | `X-Callback-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 |
| Airtel Money | `X-Airtel-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256 |

## Implementation Steps
1. Wire `verifySignature(process.env.MTN_WEBHOOK_SECRET!, 'x-callback-signature')` to the MTN route in `src/app.ts`.
2. Wire `verifySignature(process.env.AIRTEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET!, 'x-airtel-signature')` to the Airtel route.
3. For M-Pesa, implement an IP allowlist middleware reading allowed IPs from `MPESA_ALLOWED_IPS` env var.
4. Write unit tests for the middleware: valid signature passes, invalid signature returns 401, missing header returns 401.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] MTN and Airtel routes reject requests with invalid signatures.
- [ ] M-Pesa route rejects requests from non-allowlisted IPs.
- [ ] All middleware unit tests pass.
- [ ] Secrets are read from environment variables only.

title: stellar: implement Soroban settlement contract invocation
body:
## Summary
`src/stellar/settlementClient.ts` contains a stub that returns a fake tx hash. It needs to invoke the `settle` function on the deployed [MobileMoneyBridge-Contracts](https://github.com/Stellar-Project-Hub/MobileMoneyBridge-Contracts) settlement contract.

## Implementation Steps
1. Use `@stellar/stellar-sdk` `SorobanRpc.Server` and `Contract` to build a contract invocation transaction.
2. Load the keypair from `STELLAR_SECRET_KEY`.
3. Call `contract.call('settle', ...args)` with the `SettlementRequest` fields mapped to Soroban `xdr.ScVal` types.
4. Simulate the transaction first; if simulation fails, return `{ success: false, error }`.
5. Sign and submit; poll for confirmation.
6. Return `{ success: true, txHash }` on success.
7. Write a unit test that mocks `SorobanRpc.Server` and asserts the correct contract method is called.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Real Soroban contract invocation replaces the stub.
- [ ] Simulation errors are caught and returned as `SettlementResult`.
- [ ] Unit test mocks the RPC server and verifies the call.
- [ ] No secrets are logged.

title: relayer: add idempotency layer to prevent duplicate Stellar submissions
body:
## Summary
Mobile money providers may retry webhook delivery on timeout. Without idempotency, the same transaction could be submitted to Stellar multiple times.

## Implementation Steps
1. Add an in-memory `Map<string, SettlementResult>` keyed by `providerRef` (the provider's transaction ID) in `src/relayer/index.ts`.
2. Before calling `submitSettlement`, check if `providerRef` already exists in the map.
3. If it does, return the cached result immediately.
4. If not, submit and store the result.
5. Add a note in the README that this is an in-memory cache and should be replaced with Redis for production.
6. Write a test that calls `relayToStellar` twice with the same `transactionId` and asserts `submitSettlement` is only called once.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Duplicate `transactionId` calls do not trigger a second Stellar submission.
- [ ] Cached result is returned on duplicate calls.
- [ ] Test asserts `submitSettlement` mock is called exactly once.
- [ ] README documents the in-memory limitation.

title: feat: add phone number to Stellar address resolution service
body:
## Summary
The relayer currently generates stub Stellar addresses from phone numbers. A real resolution service is needed, backed by a configurable lookup (e.g., a simple key-value store or a Stellar Federation server).

## Implementation Steps
1. Create `src/utils/addressResolver.ts` exporting `resolveAddress(phone: string): Promise<string>`.
2. First, attempt a Stellar Federation lookup using `StellarSdk.Federation.resolve` if `FEDERATION_SERVER_URL` is set.
3. Fall back to a local JSON file (`address-map.json`) for development/testing.
4. Throw a descriptive error if no address is found.
5. Integrate into `src/relayer/index.ts`, replacing the stub address generation.
6. Write unit tests mocking both the federation lookup and the local file fallback.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `resolveAddress` attempts federation lookup first.
- [ ] Falls back to local map if federation is not configured.
- [ ] Throws on unresolvable phone numbers.
- [ ] Unit tests cover both paths and the error case.
- [ ] `relayToStellar` uses the real resolver.

title: feat: implement USSD session state machine for interactive payment flows
body:
## Summary
Some African mobile money flows are initiated via USSD rather than app-based STK Push. A USSD session state machine is needed to handle multi-step interactive payment confirmation.

## USSD Flow
```
Step 1: User dials *XXX# → provider sends session_id + text
Step 2: Relayer responds with payment confirmation prompt
Step 3: User enters PIN → provider sends confirmation
Step 4: Relayer triggers settlement
```

## Implementation Steps
1. Create `src/relayer/ussdSession.ts` with a `UssdSession` class.
2. State machine states: `INITIATED` → `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION` → `CONFIRMED` → `SETTLED` | `CANCELLED`.
3. Store sessions in a `Map<sessionId, UssdSession>` with a 5-minute TTL.
4. Add a POST `/webhooks/ussd` route in `src/app.ts`.
5. On each USSD callback, advance the state machine and return the appropriate USSD response string.
6. On `CONFIRMED`, call `relayToStellar`.
7. Write unit tests for each state transition, including TTL expiry.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four states are implemented and tested.
- [ ] Sessions expire after 5 minutes of inactivity.
- [ ] `CONFIRMED` state triggers `relayToStellar`.
- [ ] Invalid state transitions return an error response.
- [ ] Tests cover the full happy path and cancellation.

title: ci: add Docker build and container smoke test to CI pipeline
body:
## Summary
The CI pipeline runs lint and tests but does not verify the application can be containerised and started. A `Dockerfile` and a CI smoke test are needed.

## Implementation Steps
1. Create a `Dockerfile` using a multi-stage build:
   - Stage 1 (`builder`): `node:20-alpine`, install deps, run `npm run build`.
   - Stage 2 (`runner`): copy `dist/` and `node_modules/`, set `CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]`.
2. Create a `.dockerignore` excluding `node_modules`, `.env`, and `tests`.
3. Add a CI step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
   ```yaml
   - name: Build Docker image
     run: docker build -t mobilemoneybridge-relayer .
   - name: Smoke test
     run: |
       docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name relayer mobilemoneybridge-relayer
       sleep 3
       curl -f http://localhost:3000/health
       docker stop relayer
   ```

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `Dockerfile` builds successfully.
- [ ] `/health` endpoint responds `200` inside the container.
- [ ] CI job fails if the Docker build or smoke test fails.
- [ ] `.dockerignore` prevents secrets from being copied into the image.

title: testing: add integration test suite for all three webhook endpoints using supertest
body:
## Summary
The current test suite only covers payload parsing. Full HTTP-level integration tests using `supertest` are needed for all three webhook endpoints.

## Implementation Steps
1. Install `supertest` and `@types/supertest` as dev dependencies.
2. Create `tests/routes.test.ts`.
3. Mock `relayToStellar` using `jest.mock('../src/relayer/index')`.
4. Write tests for:
   - `POST /webhooks/mpesa` with a valid payload → `202`.
   - `POST /webhooks/mtn` with a valid payload → `202`.
   - `POST /webhooks/airtel` with a valid payload → `202`.
   - `POST /webhooks/mpesa` with a malformed body → `400` or `500`.
   - `GET /health` → `200 { status: 'ok' }`.
5. Each test must be independent; use `beforeEach` to reset mocks.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] At least 5 integration tests covering the scenarios above.
- [ ] `relayToStellar` is mocked — no real Stellar calls in tests.
- [ ] All tests pass with `npm test`.
- [ ] Coverage report shows > 70% line coverage on `src/webhooks/*.ts`.
